1. Case 1: Sepsis caused by disseminated tuberculosis
The patient's urinary symptoms and sepsis are best explained by disseminated tuberculosis with genitourinary involvement. AFB-positive urine, sputum, and FNA pus, mycobacterial growth without a pyogenic isolate, chest CT lymphadenopathy with right upper lobe consolidation, PET/CT hypermetabolic nodes, and severe inflammatory markers with acute kidney injury all converge on this diagnosis. Because GeneXpert/PCR and urinary tract imaging are still pending, confidence is high but not absolute, with nontuberculous mycobacterial infection remaining a remote alternative.
